summary: Ustaz Azlan continues the Prophet's SAW biography after the age of 20. He explains that the story of the Prophet SAW proposing to Umm Hani before his prophethood is not authentic, then tells how Khadijah RA, a wealthy and well-known merchant, offered the Prophet SAW a mudarabah partnership to take her goods to Sham, was impressed by Maisarah's report of his honesty and skill, and married him through the go-between Nafisah. The ustaz also covers Khadijah's age, their six children, the large household, a comparison with four types of jahili marriage, and the call to make marriage easy.
keyPoints: The story of the Prophet SAW proposing to Umm Hani before prophethood is not authentic; the authentic proposal came after the Conquest of Makkah and was declined because she was older with children.
Khadijah RA was a wealthy merchant who inherited from two husbands and grew her wealth through hired managers.
The Prophet SAW was chosen for his honesty and trustworthiness and sent to Sham on a 50-50 mudarabah deal together with Maisarah.
A person's real character shows when travelling, and Maisarah observed him throughout the journey.
Khadijah voiced her wish through her close friend Nafisah; Abu Talib and Hamzah carried the proposal, and the marriage had a guardian, dowry, sermon, offer and acceptance, and a feast.
The ustaz prefers the view that Khadijah was 28 when they married; they had six children.
Make marriage easy by looking for religion and character, not by piling on material expectations.

chapters.title: Introduction: four trainings before Khadijah

chapters.title: Hilf al-Fudul as a benchmark
chapters.summary: The Yemeni man's rights were returned, and Hassan ibn Ali later called for the same pact to claim his own rights.

chapters.title: The inauthentic Umm Hani proposal story
chapters.summary: The report of a proposal before prophethood is criticised by scholars; the authentic proposal came after the Conquest of Makkah and was declined.

chapters.title: Purposes of marriage in Arab culture
chapters.summary: Marriage was used to strengthen kinship, reconcile tribes and widen the reach of the call.

chapters.title: Khadijah RA: a renowned and wealthy woman
chapters.summary: Khadijah inherited from two husbands, grew the wealth through managers, and turned down prominent suitors because character mattered more than wealth.

chapters.title: Hala, the wages and a name suggested
chapters.summary: Hala told Khadijah, who was often cheated by her managers, about the Prophet's SAW honesty as a shepherd.

chapters.title: The mudarabah offer and Abu Talib's acceptance
chapters.summary: Khadijah offered a 50-50 split and Abu Talib encouraged the Prophet SAW to accept.

chapters.title: Travel reveals character
chapters.summary: A hadith on travel and the words of scholars that a journey tests and shows a person's true character.

chapters.title: The Busra trip and the doubled profit
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW finished the trade quicker and the profit doubled; Maisarah praised his character.

chapters.title: Nafisah conveys Khadijah's wish
chapters.summary: Nafisah probed with tact, and the Prophet SAW answered politely until the wish was met.

chapters.title: The proposal, dowry and marriage contract
chapters.summary: Abu Talib and Hamzah proposed, Waraqah conducted the marriage, the dowry was 20 young camels and a feast followed.

chapters.title: Khadijah's age and their children
chapters.summary: The ustaz chooses the age of 28 and lists the six children of the Prophet SAW and Khadijah.

chapters.title: The household and four jahili marriage types
chapters.summary: Ali, Zayd and Umm Ayman lived in the house; Aisha RA reported four ways of marrying in jahiliyyah.

chapters.title: Closing: make marriage easy
chapters.summary: The ustaz closes with a hadith on marrying off one whose religion and character you accept and a critique of excessive expectations.

lessons.title: Check the authenticity of sirah reports
lessons.body: The report of a proposal to Umm Hani before prophethood is rejected by scholars and cannot be accepted.

lessons.title: Marriage has social purposes
lessons.body: Marriage strengthens kinship, reconciles tribes and widens the call.

lessons.title: Character over wealth
lessons.body: Khadijah declined wealthy suitors because character is everything.

lessons.title: Honesty makes a trusted name
lessons.body: The Prophet's SAW honesty, even about his wages, led people to mention his name.

lessons.title: Mudarabah is a fair partnership
lessons.body: The investor bears the monetary loss and the worker bears the loss of time and effort.

lessons.title: Travel tests character
lessons.body: To judge someone's character, ask people who have travelled with them.

lessons.title: Assessing a prospective spouse wisely
lessons.body: Besides social media, ask the imam, teachers and friends who have travelled with the person.

lessons.title: A good friend brings good
lessons.body: Nafisah conveyed the wish with tact and protected both sides' dignity.

lessons.title: Respect family in marriage matters
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW told his uncle first, and Abu Talib and Hamzah carried the proposal.

lessons.title: Reject false stories about the Prophet's SAW marriage
lessons.body: The story that Khadijah's father was made drunk is not authentic and contradicts the Prophet's SAW character.

lessons.title: The Prophet's SAW marriage met the shariah
lessons.body: There was a guardian, dowry, sermon, offer and acceptance, and a feast.

lessons.title: Make the lawful easy and the unlawful hard
lessons.body: Do not set excessive material expectations that make marriage hard and push people toward the forbidden.

glossary.meaning: A partnership between a capital owner and a worker, with an agreed profit split and monetary loss borne by the investor.
Travel; the word is linked to 'uncovering', because a journey uncovers a person's true character.
Ijab is the offer and qabul the acceptance in a marriage contract.
The obligatory gift from husband to wife; the Prophet's SAW dowry was 20 young camels.
A jahili marriage form where the husband sent his wife to another man to obtain particular offspring.
Possessor of two lights, the title of Uthman for marrying two daughters of the Prophet SAW.
The guardian who gives a woman in marriage.

dalil.context: Linked to the fact that travel tests and reveals a person's real character.
dalil.translation: Travel is a part of torment; it keeps one from food, drink and sleep. When one has finished his purpose, let him hasten back to his family.

dalil.context: An authentic hadith showing the proposal came after the Conquest of Makkah and was declined, not before prophethood.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW proposed to Umm Hani; she replied that she was older with many children, and the Prophet SAW said the best women who ride camels are those most tender to small children and most protective of their husband's property.

dalil.context: A report scholars reject and which is not accepted because its narrators were called liars.
dalil.translation: A report from Hisham al-Kalbi that the Prophet SAW proposed to Umm Hani before prophethood, but Abu Talib married her to Hubayrah.

dalil.context: Shows the Prophet's SAW marriage to Khadijah followed the proper way, unlike jahili practices.
dalil.translation: In jahiliyyah there were four types of marriage: a man proposing to the guardian and marrying, which was how the Prophet SAW married, then istibda', group relations, and prostitution.

dalil.context: A closing reminder to make marriage easy by judging religion and character.
dalil.translation: If someone comes to you whose religion and character you are pleased with, marry him off; if not, there will be tribulation and great corruption.

sirah.era: After age 20 up to the marriage to Khadijah
sirah.summary: The Prophet SAW worked as Khadijah's trade agent, succeeded at Busra, then married Khadijah and built a large household.
